messages.subject: Downloading the 97 Links as a CSV
messages.subject_clean: Downloading the 97 Links as a CSV
messages.body_plain:
@joseph.l...@vanderbilt.edu, @mhunt...@gmail.com, @patrick...@vanderbilt.edu, and others:

Someone recently asked how to obtain the Nlsy97 links as a csv.  They spent a few minutes on our site and couldn't find it easily.

I'm posting two solutions below, but I'm a little concerned they had difficulty.  I'm open to a different organization or explanation on the site if it will help.  Or maybe there should be something on the site's front page.  However keep in mind that there are already six datasets <https://nlsy-links.github.io/NlsyLinks/reference/index.html>, and this should continue to grow.

Short answer: go to https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nlsy-links/NlsyLinks/master/outside-data/nlsy-97/links-2017-97.csv

Longer answer: go to the

 main website (https://nlsy-links.github.io/NlsyLinks/), then
“Datasets & Functions” (https://nlsy-links.github.io/NlsyLinks/reference/index.html), then
one of the two 97 datasets (either, “Links97Pair” or “Links97PairExpanded”.
Towards the bottom, each page has the following section; click on “download the csv”.  Here's what it looks like on the page:

See also

Download CSV If you're using the NlsyLinks package in R, the dataset automatically is available. To use it in a different environment, download the csv <https://github.com/nlsy-links/NlsyLinks/blob/master/outside-data/nlsy-79/links-2017-79.csv?raw=true>, which is readable by all statistical software. links-metadata-2017-97.yml <https://github.com/nlsy-links/NlsyLinks/blob/master/outside-data/nlsy-97/links-metadata-2017-97.yml> documents the dataset version information.
